moving.setup.title: Already use Nocturne on your phone?
moving.receive.countsUndated: {count, plural, one {# thing kept} other {# things kept}} · about {size}
moving.receive.room: This computer needs about {size} free for it and has {free}. Free some room here, then choose {moveItHere}.
moving.choose.title: {name} has its own memory, and this computer has one too.
moving.choose.counts: {count, plural, one {# thing kept on {name} since {date}} other {# things kept on {name} since {date}}} · about {size}
moving.choose.lead: A computer holds one person’s memory. Choose how {name} joins this one.
moving.choose.bring.hint: What was kept on {name}, with its journal and check-ins, joins the memory here, and Nocturne reads it as new. Its calendar and health readings are sent again, with nothing doubled.
moving.choose.use.hint: Nothing comes in from {name}. It works with this computer like your other phones, and what it holds now is put aside on it.
moving.bring.adding: Adding them to the memory here…
moving.bring.stopAsk: Stop bringing them in? Nothing changes here, and {name} keeps its memory.
moving.brought.title: {name}’s things are here.
moving.brought.body: {count, plural, one {# thing} other {# things}}, {entries, plural, one {# journal entry} other {# journal entries}} and {checkins, plural, one {# check-in} other {# check-ins}} were added. Nocturne reads them as new over the next while; finding them by their words works now.
moving.brought.removed: {name} was removed while they were added, so it still holds its own memory.
moving.ended.removed: {name} was removed, so nothing came in from it.
moving.ended.stopped: {name} stopped bringing its things in. Nothing changed here.
moving.used.title: {name} now works with this computer.
moving.used.body: Nothing came in from it. Its calendar and health come here from now on.
moving.failed.room: There wasn’t room for {name}’s memory, so nothing changed. Free about {size} here, then move it again from {name}.
moving.phone.found.title: Move your memory to {computer}?
moving.phone.found.lead: {computer} becomes the home of your memory. It reads, tidies and writes your page from now on.
moving.phone.found.then: This phone then works with {computer}: keep, ask and read your page from here.
moving.phone.found.one: Your memory lives in one place at a time, so it moves rather than copies.
moving.phone.waiting.title: {computer} already holds a memory.
moving.phone.waiting.body: Choose on {computer} what happens to yours. Nothing changes until you do.
moving.phone.size.title: What moves
moving.phone.size.kept: {count, plural, one {# thing you kept since {date}} other {# things you kept since {date}}}
moving.phone.size.journal: {count, plural, one {# journal entry} other {# journal entries}}
moving.phone.size.bytes: About {size}, most of it photos and recordings
moving.phone.size.open: Keep Nocturne open; it carries on if the phone allows.
moving.phone.size.after: Your memory here is put aside once it has arrived. You choose then whether to remove it.
moving.phone.moving.title: Moving your memory
moving.phone.moving.preparing: Getting your memory ready to move…
moving.phone.moving.left: {minutes, plural, one {About # minute left} other {About # minutes left}}
moving.phone.moving.note: You can still keep things. They go across at the end.
moving.phone.moving.stopAsk: Stop moving? Nothing has changed here, and {computer} keeps nothing of it.
moving.phone.bringing.title: Bringing your things to {computer}
moving.phone.bringing.adding: Adding them to the memory on {computer}…
moving.phone.bringing.stopAsk: Stop bringing your things in? Nothing changes on {computer}, and your memory stays on this phone.
moving.phone.paused: Moving paused. It carries on when {computer} is back.
moving.phone.notWhole: Something didn’t arrive whole, so nothing changed. Try again.
moving.phone.outdated: Update Nocturne on {computer}, then try again. Nothing was changed.
moving.phone.noRoom: {computer} needs more free room for your memory. Free some there, then try again.
moving.phone.ranOut: {computer} ran out of room, so nothing changed. Your memory is still on this phone.
moving.phone.stoppedThere: {computer} stopped the move. Nothing changed, and your memory is still on this phone.
moving.phone.moved.keep: Keep it put aside for 30 days
moving.phone.brought.title: Your things are on {computer}.
moving.phone.brought.body: {count, plural, one {# thing} other {# things}}, {entries, plural, one {# journal entry} other {# journal entries}} and {checkins, plural, one {# check-in} other {# check-ins}} were added to the memory there. {computer} reads them over the next while. This phone now works with {computer}.
moving.phone.used.title: This phone now works with {computer}.
moving.phone.used.body: Nothing went to {computer}. What this phone held is put aside here, and its calendar and health go to {computer} from now on.
moving.phone.used.warning: Nothing from this phone went to {computer}, so removing it deletes it for good.
moving.phone.aside.bringAsk: Bring the things put aside {day} to {computer}?
moving.phone.aside.bringBody: {things, plural, one {# thing} other {# things}} kept, {entries, plural, one {# journal entry} other {# journal entries}} and {checkins, plural, one {# check-in} other {# check-ins}} join the memory on {computer}, which reads them as new. What is put aside here stays until you remove it.
moving.phone.aside.removeBody: Its things are on {computer} now. This removes the copy left on this phone.
moving.phone.aside.removeWriting: Pages and reflections written on this phone go with it.
moving.phone.aside.deleteAsk: Delete what was put aside {day} for good?
moving.phone.aside.deleteBody: Nothing from it went to {computer}. This deletes {things, plural, one {# thing} other {# things}} kept, {entries, plural, one {# journal entry} other {# journal entries}} and {media, plural, one {# photo or recording} other {# photos and recordings}}, and they can’t be brought back.
